blocks.text: About Hollowell Patent Group PLLC

We prepare and prosecute patent applications, review and maintain the portfolios that result, and advise clients on patents held by others when a product decision or a dispute depends on them. Our technical work is concentrated in medical devices, in inventions that originate in university research, and in the electrical and embedded hardware that early-stage companies build, and each matter is staffed by attorneys and patent agents trained in the field at issue.

This overview sets out the services we provide, the terms on which we accept a matter, and some of the clients whose matters we have completed. It is written for prospective clients and for the advisers who refer them, and it is revised whenever the practice changes in a way a client would need to know.
Services
The practice is organized into the service lines below. A client who uses more than one of them signs a separate engagement letter for each, with its own scope, its own staff, and its own fee.

items: Prosecution. We take an invention from the inventor's first written description to an issued patent, and we plan the filings that follow it so that later claims keep pace with the product as it changes.

Portfolio review. A structured written review of a client's holdings, organized by patent family, that records the status of each application and patent, the costs coming due to keep it in force, and whether its claims still read on what the client sells.
Freedom-to-operate and validity opinions. Privileged written analysis of third-party patents for a client preparing a launch, considering a design change, or answering a demand letter.

Challenges to issued patents. Advice on whether to petition for review of a competitor's patent before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board, and the defense of a client's own patents when another party petitions against them.
Board and investor summaries. A short presentation that puts a portfolio on one page for a board of directors or for an investor conducting diligence.

Accepting a matter

A matter is accepted only after a conflicts search covering each party the prospective client names, including affiliates and co-owners of the technology, and we decline the matter if that search does not clear. The engagement letter then fixes the scope, lists what is excluded from it, sets the billing basis, and explains the consequences of nonpayment, and we do not begin work on the merits until the client has countersigned it.

Each matter has one responsible attorney or agent, named in the engagement letter, who answers for its deadlines and its correspondence. Between deliverables, that person writes to the client briefly, under the matter's docket number, whenever something has been filed, received from the patent office, or set for a response. We bill by the matter, and the fee basis for each one is stated in its engagement letter before any work is done.
Deadlines

A missed date is the one error a patent practice cannot correct after the fact, and the firm is run accordingly. Each statutory, response, and maintenance date is entered when it first arises, checked against the official record by a second person, and assigned to the responsible attorney or agent, and any reminder that goes unacknowledged is escalated to a partner.
Written advice

Opinions on infringement and validity are written to the standard a court or an investor might later apply to them. Each one defines its scope before anything else, identifies what was reviewed and what was not, and states no conclusion more firmly than the analysis supports; each carries a privilege legend at the head of the opening page and is checked by a partner before it is sent.
Contact

Inquiries about new matters are handled by Mary Bradley, Managing Partner. The first step for a prospective client is a short written description of the technology and of the parties involved, sent to Mary Bradley, who will open a conflicts search on receipt.

Welcome and first-period record: Matthew Parrish

Matthew Parrish has now completed his first week as a member of the Prosecution group, where he holds the title of Patent Agent, and the firm is pleased to have him. He was hired principally for search work, and in the ordinary course he will run the prior art searches that support new applications and opinions and prepare the first draft of the landscape tables that go into our portfolio reviews. His first assignments will come from matters already open in the group, so that he learns the firm's search conventions on work whose scope has been settled.

Matthew reports to Heather Munoz, Partner. She hands out his searches, sets the scope of each one in writing before he begins, and checks the results before any of them are relied on in a filing or a memorandum. His search results go to the responsible attorney and not directly to the client, and each write-up should state which collections, classifications, and date ranges were searched and where coverage may be thin, because the attorney who signs an opinion has to know the limits of the search beneath it. He has said that he would rather leave client-facing drafting to the attorneys, and that suits the role as the firm has defined it.

His workstation, building access card, and logins for the docket and the document management system were in place on his first day, and he has signed the confidentiality agreement and listed his prior employers and personal holdings for the conflicts file. Every search is opened under the client's matter number so that his time is recorded against the right matter, and any date he comes across in the course of a search, such as a response period in a related family, goes to docketing the same day it is found. Database charges are booked to the matter as well, and a search that looks likely to run past its estimate should be raised with Heather Munoz before it does.

Mary Bradley will sit down with Matthew and Heather Munoz together once he has finished his first full portfolio landscape, to decide which kinds of search he can then take on with only spot review. Before anything else, he and Heather Munoz will agree the written scope of his first search, and he will run no query until that is done.
David Chang: record of onboarding

This record covers the start of David Chang's time with the firm, now one week in, as one of the Patent Agents in Prosecution, and it sets down his role, his reporting line, and what is expected of him over his first period. His matters will be drawn mainly from electrical and embedded-systems applications, where the claims depend on how the hardware and its firmware actually behave. He will also be asked from time to time to read a colleague's draft where a claim turns on firmware behavior, and that reading is advisory, with the responsible attorney or agent keeping the decision.

David reports to Heather Munoz, Partner, and his matters come to him from her, as does the review of each new application and each office action response before it is filed. He prefers to settle a disputed claim interpretation with the examiner by telephone before committing a position to writing, which the firm encourages, and every such interview is to be summarized in the file on the day it takes place and copied to Heather Munoz.

Patent agents at this firm prosecute applications; opinions on infringement or validity belong to counsel and are signed by an attorney, so when a client asks David for a view of that kind, he should say that he will put the question to the responsible attorney and then do so the same day. Over the coming weeks, the work is divided as follows:

items: David Chang: return his conflicts disclosure and the firm's confidentiality agreement, spend a morning with docketing to learn how dates are entered and verified, and acknowledge each docket reminder in writing when it reaches him.
Heather Munoz: choose the matters he starts on, read every application and response before it is filed, and decide when that reading can be narrowed.
Mary Bradley: review his progress with Heather Munoz once his first responses have been filed, and confirm his matter assignments for the period that follows.

blocks.text: His accounts, building access, and workstation are already set up, and his time is to be recorded daily against each matter number, since the firm bills by the matter and a client is entitled to see where the hours went. The next step is for David to take over the office action responses that Heather Munoz has set aside for him, beginning with the one whose response date falls first.
Everyone,

Our outside IT support will take the file server and the document management system offline tomorrow evening for updates and a backup test. The work begins after close of business and is expected to finish overnight. The docket system runs on the same server, so it will be unavailable as well. Email will stay up throughout.

Before you leave tomorrow, save and close your open documents, log out of the docket system, and print the reminders you will need for the rest of the week. I am the office contact for the work this week. If a filing has to go out during the window, tell me by noon tomorrow so the start can be moved.
Sincerely
Hollowell Patent Group PLLC
Firm overview

We are a patent boutique. Our attorneys and patent agents prepare and prosecute applications, manage the portfolios those applications become, and give written advice on third-party patents when a client's product or a pending dispute turns on them, with most of our technical work in medical devices, in electrical and embedded systems, and in inventions that begin in university laboratories.

Each matter is staffed with people trained in the relevant technology. Each also has a single named attorney or agent who answers for its dates and its correspondence from the day it opens until the day it closes.
Practice areas
The table below summarizes the kinds of matter we take on and what a client has in hand when each one is complete.

rows: Applications drafted from the inventor's disclosure, responses to office actions, examiner interviews, and a filing plan for continuations as the product develops
A written review, family by family, of where each asset stands, what it will cost to keep in force, and how closely its claims track current products
A privileged memorandum that defines its scope first, distinguishes established findings from open questions, and qualifies its conclusions to match
Searches and a written assessment ahead of a product release, covering the technology and, where the client asks, the proposed product name
An assessment of whether to challenge a competitor's patent after grant, and representation of the client when its issued patents are challenged
A short deck that summarizes the whole portfolio on a single slide for directors or investors

Opening a matter

We open a matter in three steps, in this order: a conflicts search across every party the client identifies, an engagement letter that sets out the scope, the exclusions, the billing basis, and what happens on nonpayment, and the client's countersignature on that letter. Nothing substantive is done before the third step, because work performed before the scope is agreed is work the client has not authorized.

On nonpayment the letter is specific: it states when work on the matter stops and when we will withdraw from it, where the professional rules permit withdrawal, and we follow that provision as written. Clients are told this at the outset so that it never comes as a surprise.
Correspondence

Routine news on a matter, such as a filing made, an office action received, or a response period opened, reaches the client as a short email that cites the docket number. Longer work arrives as a written deliverable organized under headings, identifying by name and title every attorney and agent who worked on it, and an opinion is marked as privileged and goes out only after a partner has reviewed it.
Docketing

Every date on which a client's rights depend, whether a statutory bar, a response period, or a maintenance payment, is entered as soon as it arises and verified a second time, by someone other than the person who entered it, against what the patent office shows. The responsible attorney or agent acknowledges each reminder in writing, and a reminder left unacknowledged goes to a partner the same day.
How to reach us

Mary Bradley, Managing Partner, handles inquiries about new matters. Anyone considering the firm for a new matter should begin with a brief note to her identifying the client, any co-owner of the technology, and any party the client expects to be adverse, after which she will confirm whether the firm is free to act before a first call is scheduled.
